title: Preparing a Debate Outline
text:
A debate outline is a plan that helps a speaker organize their arguments before a competition begins. It usually starts with a clear statement of the motion and a short definition of the key terms. After that, the speaker lists two or three main points, and each point is supported by evidence such as facts, examples, or expert opinions. A good outline also anticipates the opposing side's arguments.

Many students find it useful to write their outline on a single page, because it keeps them focused during the debate. Some speakers use colored notes to mark each main point, which makes it easier to find information quickly. However, an outline should never be read word for word, since judges can tell when a speaker is not really thinking. Instead, it should work as a guide that supports natural and confident speaking.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does a debate outline usually begin with?
options: A clear statement of the motion and definitions of key terms
A list of the judges' names
A summary of the final result
A long story about the speaker's life

questions.text: On how many pages do many students find it useful to write their outline?
Why would a speaker who reads the outline word for word probably be judged negatively?
options: Reading word for word makes the speaker's arguments shorter
Judges can tell the speaker is not really thinking
The outline is too short to be read aloud
Colored notes are not allowed during a debate

questions.text: What can be inferred about the purpose of the evidence in a debate outline?
options: It helps make each main point convincing
It replaces the need for a clear motion
It is only needed by the judges
It should be memorized in full

vocabulary.definition: a plan or summary of the main points
expects something and prepares for it before it happens
facts or examples that support an argument
sure of yourself and your abilities

paragraph_translations: Um esboço de debate é um plano que ajuda o orador a organizar seus argumentos antes do início de uma competição. Geralmente, começa com uma declaração clara da moção e uma definição curta dos termos principais. Depois disso, o orador lista dois ou três pontos principais, e cada ponto é apoiado por evidências, como fatos, exemplos ou opiniões de especialistas. Um bom esboço também antecipa os argumentos do lado oposto.

Muitos alunos acham útil escrever o esboço em uma única página, porque isso os mantém focados durante o debate. Alguns oradores usam anotações coloridas para marcar cada ponto principal, o que facilita encontrar informações rapidamente. No entanto, um esboço nunca deve ser lido palavra por palavra, pois os juízes percebem quando o orador não está realmente pensando. Em vez disso, ele deve funcionar como um guia que apoie uma fala natural e confiante.
